title: Bridgeway Pilot Orientation & Success Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook scopes the 6-week Bridgeway pilot (Bridgeway is a mid-market fintech customer). It combines the kickoff agenda, technical onboarding checklist, measurable success criteria, and an operational runbook for early rollouts. Aim is to validate that Redwood can meet Bridgeway's latency, cost, and data isolation requirements in a production-like environment and produce a clear go/no-go decision at the end of the pilot.

Background:
- Customer: Bridgeway Financial Services (payments + reconciliation workloads).
- Use case: in-chat assistant for transaction triage and automated reconciliation suggestions, plus nightly bulk embeddings for similarity search.
- Main constraints: sensitive PII in prompts and backend storage, strict audit requirements, and peak-hour burst traffic during reconciliation windows.
- Desired outcome: demonstrable end-to-end inference flow with SLOs met, regression-free outputs on the provided promptset, and operational playbooks for Dedicated or Private deployment.

Objectives (success-driven):
1) Functional: Integrate Redwood API with Bridgeway staging environment and validate feature parity for chat and embeddings.
2) Performance: P95 generation latency <= 350ms for typical prompt length (≤ 256 tokens) and sustained throughput of 300 requests/min with autoscale profiles.
3) Cost: Achieve a measured per-1k-token cost within 25% of projected estimate in the cost model.
4) Security & Compliance: KV-cache and logs encrypted, audit logs delivered to Bridgeway S3 cross-account, and KMS integration validated.
5) Quality: Pass evaluation suite with minimum 85% topical accuracy and no high-severity hallucination cases on the 200-prompt QA set.

Kickoff workshop agenda (90m):
- 0–10m Introductions & pilot goals (owner + AC)
- 10–25m High-level architecture walkthrough (redwood engineer)
- 25–40m Data privacy and network controls (SRE + security)
- 40–60m Acceptance criteria walkthrough & evaluation rubric (product)
- 60–80m Operational plan: canary, rollback, alerting thresholds (SRE)
- 80–90m Next steps, action item capture, owners & dates

Roles & responsibilities:
- Bridgeway PM: product decisions, promptset owner
- Bridgeway Infra: grant VPC peering / cross-account S3 access
- Redwood Solutions Eng (Aisha): technical lead, integration checkpoints, demo owner
- Redwood SRE (Marco): perf runs, alerting, rollout policy author
- Redwood Security (Evelyn): KMS audit, data handling checklist

Technical onboarding checklist (must be completed in week 1):
- Verify staging VPC peering and egress rules for telemetry endpoints
- KMS key exchange and grant policies (test encryption roundtrip)
- Configure audit log sink to Bridgeway S3 (verify deliveries for last 7 days)
- Provision test model variants: baseline-7B-qa (quantized) and baseline-13B-balanced
- Wire sample prompt adapter and embed pipeline (nightly job skeleton)
- Set up prefix/KV cache policy for reconciliation prompts (cache warmers enabled)
- Create secrets in Bridgeway vault and rotate keys in 30d simulation

Performance validation plan:
- Synthetic load tool: prompter-bench (scripts in linked_artifacts repo)
- Test scenarios: steady-state 300 req/min; burst 900 req/min for 5m windows to simulate reconciliation windows
- Metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, error rate, autoscale spin-up time, cost per 1k tokens
- Acceptance: p95 <= 350ms for typical prompts on baseline-13B-balanced when under steady-state; error rate < 0.5%

Quality evaluation rubric (promptset and grading):
- Promptset: 200 hand-curated prompts from Bridgeway (mix of short triage queries and long reconciliation contexts)
- Grading axes: topical accuracy (binary), helpfulness (0–3), hallucination severity (none/low/medium/high), response length correctness
- Pass condition: >=85% topical accuracy AND no more than 2 high-severity hallucination incidents in the full set

Acceptance tests (end-of-pilot go/no-go):
- End-to-end demo: Bridgeway team can trigger use cases from staging UI and observe correct assistant behavior for 10 representative scenarios
- SLO compliance: performance and error budgets met for 7 consecutive days under synthetic steady-state traffic
- Security: KMS keys audited, audit log deliveries validated, and data flow diagram approved by Bridgeway security
- Cost reconciliation: actual spend within agreed variance of forecast model

Operational runbook snippets:
- Canary deployment flow: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with 30m observation windows; automatic rollback on p95 spike > 2x baseline or error > 1%
- Alerts to create: latency_p95_above_threshold, error_rate_trend_up, autoscale_fail, audit_log_delivery_failure
- For audit_log_delivery_failure: immediate: notify SRE and security, create incident ticket, remediate S3 permissions and re-run delivery test script

Data handling and security notes:
- All PII must be redacted before persistent storage. Bridgeway will provide a redaction lambda; Redwood will mark caches ephemeral and exclude from persistent logs where feasible.
- Cross-account S3 deliveries must include encryption-at-rest and object-level logging. Audit trail retention set to 365 days for pilot.
- Temporary exception: for debugging only, a time-limited logging flag can be enabled by Aisha and Evelyn with approval; logs automatically purged after 72 hours.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: peak bursts exceed Dedicated capacity leading to degraded latency. Mitigation: enable burst buffer pool and temporary routing to hosted fallback with lower-cost model variant + customer-facing degraded-mode message.
- Risk: QA shows systematic hallucinations on reconciliation line-items. Mitigation: pause canary, run targeted prompt engineering session with Bridgeway, deploy constrained decoding and recalibrate temperature.
- Risk: audit logs delayed. Mitigation: alternate delivery to Bridgeway's secure FTP as a fallback and escalate with infra team.

Deliverables & timetable (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): access and agreements signed, promptset & sample data provided
- Week 1: env setup, KMS, VPC peering, deploy baseline model variants
- Week 2: integration tests, embed pipeline, QA smoke tests
- Week 3: performance tuning, autoscale policy adjustments, start 7-day steady-state collection
- Week 4: evaluation run, fix issues, second QA pass
- Week 5: canary rollout in Bridgeway staging, validate audit logs and runbook
- Week 6: executive demo + decision: go to Dedicated/private or iterate (deliver final report)

Success sign-off criteria (signature required from Bridgeway PM + Redwood Solutions Lead and Redwood Security):
- All acceptance tests green
- Open issues <= 3 low-priority items with remediation plan
- Cost projection agreed and procurement path identified

Open action items after kickoff: (initial owners and ETA)
- Bridgeway: share sanitized promptset (owner: Bridgeway PM, due: 2025-09-15)
- Redwood SRE: run initial prompter-bench script and share baseline report (owner: Marco, due: 2025-09-19)
- Security: finalize KMS key policy and verify cross-account grant (owner: Evelyn, due: 2025-09-18)
- Solutions Eng: wire up audit log sink and validate deliveries (owner: Aisha, due: 2025-09-20)

Notes from kickoff discussion (raw, unedited):
- Bridgeway: prefer Dedicated but wants to see pilot numbers before committing. Concerned about cost during end-of-month reconciliation spikes.
- Suggestion: add a cost-threshold automatic throttle that pauses non-critical embedding batches during cost spikes.
- Action: schedule 90m prompt-tuning workshop in week 2 (owner: Aisha + Bridgeway PM).

Appendix: quick checklists and useful commands
- prompter-bench run: ./tools/prompter-bench --profile bridgeway-staging --duration 7200s --burst 900
- log delivery test: ./infra/check-s3-delivery.sh --bucket bridgeway-audit --days 7
- KMS policy validate: aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <bridgeway-key> --policy-name default

Document version notes: draft v0.3 — this is a working playbook intended to be iterated during the pilot.
notes: Informal kickoff notes included; expect updates post-week-1. Stored under shared drive for collaboration and quick edits.
